info.title: drymem
info.description:
Shared long-term memory for AI coding agents.

Every memory belongs to a project, identified by its normalised git remote, and
to the person who saved it. Memories are private until explicitly promoted.

get.description:
Unauthenticated on purpose: the sign-in page needs to know whether to
offer 'create your organisation' or 'sign in'.

post.description: Only while the server is empty. The first person owns the organisation.

Set or change your own password. A user who has none yet (created by
`drymem-admin` before identity existed) may set one without a current.

post.description: For CI and other machines. Shown once; `drymem login` is the human path.
Step one of `drymem login`. Unauthenticated: the CLI has nothing yet.
Step two, in the browser, signed in.
Step three: the CLI collects its token. Handed over exactly once.
Save a session summary. Returns 422 if it contains a private key.

patch.description:
Append to a topic, or replace it.

Appending is the default because Graphiti reconciles contradictions itself:
the older fact is marked superseded rather than lost, which keeps the history
of a decision readable.

get.description: Every topic key already stored. Used by `drymem import` to stay idempotent.

delete.description: Delete a memory. A uuid outside the caller's org is simply not found.

post.description:
Record whether a retrieved memory was useful.

This is the pilot's precision metric: PLAN.md's 90% bar is measured from
these rows, so the query that surfaced the memory is stored alongside the
thumb — a rating with no query cannot be learned from.

Share a memory with the project's members.

Only your own memory, and only into a project you belong to. Promoting an
already-promoted memory succeeds without duplicating it, so a retry is safe.
Add someone to a project. They see its team memories, never its private ones.

get.description:
Subjects the team's memories keep returning to.

Which of them lack a skill is decided by the client, which is the only side
that knows what is installed on this machine.

post.description:
Draft a SKILL.md from the memories about a subject.

The result is a draft for a person to review, never something installed
automatically: a skill changes how every agent on the team behaves.

get.description:
What a well-written memory looks like.

Served rather than duplicated in each client: the UI, the CLI and any future
editor plugin all need the same list, and three hand-copied lists drift.
The sittings this project's memories came out of.
Everyone in this org, with counts only — never anyone's memories.

post.description: Publish a reviewed draft to the project. Publishing twice replaces it.

get.description: Who this token belongs to. The UI needs it to say 'you' anywhere.

patch.description: Set your display name. An empty name falls back to your email.

delete.description: Take someone off a project. Their own memories stay theirs and stay private.

patch.description:
Give a project a readable name.

Declared *after* the member routes on purpose: `project_key` is a `:path`
converter, so registered first it would greedily match
`/v1/projects/<key>/members/<email>` as a project named
"<key>/members/<email>". The key itself never changes — it is the normalised
git remote, and changing it would split the team's memory in two.

get.description: Everything the dashboard opens with, in one round trip.
Liveness for both stores. Unauthenticated on purpose — it reveals nothing.
